blocks.source: Vol III, Tool Calling, § Tool Subsystem Architecture
blocks.md: When the socket times out on `restart_container`, a runtime that drops the failed call from history or reports it as a clean failure invites the next model turn to issue a duplicate restart. @Lst-vol3-tool-call-turn shows the staging restart as one turn of the loop, in a provider-neutral form. The runtime reports what it knows about this attempt, and the next model call receives that result together with the earlier request and proposal.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Computer-use tool calls matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A click keeps every tool-boundary invariant while losing atomicity, so each observation carries capture, window, and coordinate mapping and target identity is rechecked before dispatch.

questions.q: The section **Tool Subsystem Architecture** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Which descriptors the model sees each turn and how much work each tool does are design variables priced in context tokens and in cost per accepted task.
Capture and staging are separate budgets, so the adapter drains both pipes, enforces byte limits, and stages a head-and-tail view with a typed notice of what was omitted and a handle to the rest.
Read, set-desired-state, and produce-another-event classify what a repeated call does, a dimension orthogonal to the authority levels.
A click keeps every tool-boundary invariant while losing atomicity, so each observation carries capture, window, and coordinate mapping and target identity is rechecked before dispatch.
